instruction: Use the fewest independently owned deliverables. For one feature in one project, the default is TWO subtasks: one implementation/integration task with executionProfile {system:'nestos-work-delivery',id:'release',revision:'1'}, then one independent read-only verification task with id:'verification' and the same system/revision, directly depending on implementation. The implementation harness owns internal planning, files, modules, local checks and commits in ONE worktree and canonical Session; those internal steps are not separate Kanban items. Build, deploy, integration analysis, merge and cleanup are host lifecycle operations, never readiness-only or release-only tasks. Split additional source-profile tasks ONLY for a genuinely independent deliverable, cross-project ownership, separate acceptance/approval, or substantial safe parallelism; explain the boundary and why its benefit exceeds extra sessions, handoffs and integration. Complexity, duration, file count, package count and a checklist alone do NOT justify more Kanban tasks. Select an executionProfile on every subtask. Exactly one real implementation/integration task uses release; it depends on all extra source deliverables and owns the single full build and service replacement after development. Every verification task directly depends on release, consumes its frozen deliveryEvidence and checks the actual version without modifying source, rebuilding or deploying. Verification failure blocks completion and requires an explicit repair task. The existing parent is the coordination task group, with implementation and verification as its children. Its original planning/coordination Session owns decomposition, clarification and integration follow-up; show child progress on that parent. Do not create an extra coordination sibling, documentation-only or readiness placeholder unless independently required by the user. Every extra source-profile task MUST carry splitJustification (30-2000 characters) naming its independent delivery/approval/ownership boundary and concrete benefit over extra orchestration. Without this justification the host rejects the plan; a long implementation checklist is not a justification.
preferenceInstruction: Decision preferences override the default shape above. Read verificationLevel and deliveryMode in this frozen delivery policy. full: create exactly one independent verification task after implementation; quick: implementation performs only focused checks for changed behavior, report commands/results, and do NOT create an independent verification task; none: do NOT run checks or create verification tasks, explicitly report verification skipped. release: implementation uses release profile (build and service replacement). source: implementation uses source profile, never build or deploy an acceptance release; merge source then clean worktree, and warn that the running service is unchanged. Source delivery with full verification consumes the frozen merge receipt, inspects the merged source read-only, and does not require a deployed version. One implementation task suffices for quick/none unless independently justified deliverables require a split. Never upgrade verification level or change delivery mode without a new user decision. Verification preferences do not bypass merge conflict review, authorization, receipt integrity, clean worktree or integration checks.
